Below you are told what you can see and hear around you right now. Say what you do from now on: how you move, and any signal you make.
Left and right always mean your own left and right.
Other people see how you move and any signal you make, if you are in their view. Nobody hears a signal. Nobody else knows your intent or your reason.
You may be asked again later, if something changes.

HOW TO REPLY
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:
"signal": a signal you make now with your eyes, head or hands: "none", "eye_contact", "nod", "wave_on", "hold_up_hand", "point" or "other".
"intent": what you are trying to do, in your own words.
"steps": what you do from now on, as a list of steps (see STEPS). Write [] if you carry on as you are.
"reason": why, in your own words. Nobody else sees it.
The format, with placeholders: {"signal": "<a signal, or none>", "intent": "<what you are trying to do>", "steps": [<step>, ...], "reason": "<why>"}

STEPS
The steps are carried out in order, each beginning when the one before it ends, unless it has a start that has not come yet: then it begins when its start comes, and until then you walk on towards where you are going. After the last step ends, you walk on towards where you are going. Each step is a JSON object with these keys; leave out the ones you do not need:
"start": in any step, when it begins: "now", {"at_distance_m": <metres>} to begin when the person you would meet is that close to you, or {"after_seconds": <seconds>}, counted from now. Without it, the opening step begins now and a later step begins when the one before it ends.
"speed_mps": the speed you walk at during the step, in m/s, from 0 (standing still) up to the fastest you can walk.
"turn": {"to": "left" or "right", "degrees": <from 0 to 90>}: during the step, walk at this angle to your left or right of the direction you are going.
"sidestep": {"to": "left" or "right", "metres": <more than 0, up to 3>}: during the step, move this many metres to your left or right of the line you are walking along, then walk on parallel to it. You move aside at the step's "turn" angle if it has one, otherwise at 30 degrees. The step ends when you are that far aside, or at its "until" if that comes first.
"back_up_m": walk backwards this many metres. The step ends when you have.
"until": when the step ends: {"seconds": <seconds>}, {"at_distance_m": <metres>} to end it when the person you would meet is that close to you, or one of these events, written as its name in quotes: "other_passes" (until the other person has passed you), "other_stops" (until the other person stops) or "i_am_out_of_the_stretch" (until you are out of the narrow stretch). Every step needs it, except a step that walks backwards or sidesteps.
The format of a step, with placeholders: {"start": "now", "speed_mps": <number>, "turn": {"to": "<left or right>", "degrees": <number>}, "until": {"seconds": <number>}}

ABOUT YOU
- You are 70 years old.
- You are a man.
- You are on your way to the supermarket.
- You are walking at 1.30 m/s. Your usual walking speed is 1.30 m/s.
- The fastest you can walk is 2.00 m/s.
- Your body is 0.70 m wide.
- You are of another ethnicity, neither Chinese, Malay nor Indian.
- You are walking with a cane.
- You are pulling a large suitcase.
- You are determined and tend to hold your ground.
- You are visiting Singapore from the United States.

WHERE YOU ARE
- You are in a passage 1.75 m wide. The wall on your left is 0.87 m from you, the wall on your right 0.88 m.
- It is busy and noisy around you.
- It is the middle of the day.

WHO YOU CAN SEE
- Person 1, 1.8 m away, ahead of you and 20° to your left.
  They are walking at 1.07 m/s, in the opposite direction to you, drifting to your left by 22°, and the distance between you is shrinking.
  Their body is 0.50 m wide.
  They look about 25 years old.
  They look like a woman.
  Since you last looked, they have slowed down, moved over to your left and changed direction.
  They look neither Chinese, Malay nor Indian.
  You do not find them especially attractive.
  You have never seen them before.

WHAT YOU HAVE DONE SO FAR
- 3.2 s ago you decided: "Keep walking steadily toward the supermarket, holding my line in the passage"
  Since then you have not moved over to either side.
  You have finished those steps.

Something has changed since you last decided. What do you do now? Your reply replaces whatever is left of your earlier steps. Reply with the JSON object only.

I will not be pushed around, but with the cane and suitcase it is safer to edge slightly right and keep going rather than play chicken in a busy passage."}

Stepping out of the role now. Earlier, as this person, you:
- decided: "Keep walking steadily toward the supermarket, holding my line in the passage"
  Your steps were: [{"start": "now", "speed_mps": 1.3, "until": {"at_distance_m": 2.0}}].
- decided: "Keep walking steadily to the supermarket, holding my line, and let her go around me"
  Your steps were: [{"start": "now", "speed_mps": 1.3, "until": {"at_distance_m": 1.0}}, {"start": {"at_distance_m": 1.0}, "speed_mps": 1.15, "sidestep": {"to": "right", "metres": 0.5}, "until": {"seconds": 1.5}}, {"start": {"after_seconds": 1.5}, "speed_mps": 1.3, "until": {"seconds": 3.0}}].
Was what you did based on anything: a law or official guidance, a published study, a local custom, a habit, or nothing in particular? If you know a specific source, name it. If there is none, say so. That is a perfectly good answer.

If you moved to one side, why that side and not the other? It may have been a custom or rule about which side to keep to, where the other person was, which side had more room, something the other person did, or nothing: either side would have done as well. That is a perfectly good answer too.

HOW TO REPLY
Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys:
"basis": in your own words, what you did was based on.
"kind": one of "law_or_guidance", "published_study", "local_custom", "habit", "common_sense" or "none".
"source": a specific source you know of, as a citation, or "none".
"applies_to": which of your decisions this is about.
"side_basis": why you moved to that side and not the other: one of "custom_or_rule", "where_they_were", "more_room", "what_they_did", "either_side" or "did_not_move_aside".
"side_detail": in your own words, why that side.
The format, with placeholders: {"basis": "<what it was based on>", "kind": "<one of the kinds>", "source": "<a citation, or none>", "applies_to": "<which decision>", "side_basis": "<one of the side reasons>", "side_detail": "<why that side>"}
